findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: In EventManager.create, mainHostDestinationCalendar can be undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array. The condition checks mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so bookings/reschedules with Google Meet selected and no destination calendar throw a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when the main destination calendar is null
findings.body: handleNewBooking initializes evt.destinationCalendar as null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. It then uses evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars), so if it is null the collected team/host destination calendars are silently discarded. Collective events with an organizer who has no destination calendar will not create calendar events for other hosts.

findings.title: updateLocation creates references without calendar credential/external IDs
findings.body: EventManager.updateLocation maps update results to referencesToCreate using result.externalId and result.credentialId, but CalendarManager.updateEvent does not set these fields on successful update results. It also uses result.createdEvent, while update results contain updatedEvent. As a result, references created after editing a location can have empty uid and undefined credentialId/externalCalendarId, breaking later calendar updates/cancellations.

findings.title: Google updateEvent fallback cannot select a calendar when externalCalendarId is missing
findings.body: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent, selectedCalendar is set to externalCalendarId if truthy; otherwise it searches event.destinationCalendar for a calendar whose externalId === externalCalendarId. When externalCalendarId is null/undefined, this comparison can never match, so selectedCalendar becomes undefined and the Google Calendar API update is called with an undefined calendarId. This breaks updates/reschedules for older references that lack externalCalendarId.

findings.title: Google createEvent patch can use undefined calendarId
findings.body: GoogleCalendarService.createEvent inserts the event with calendarId: selectedCalendar || 'primary', but the follow-up patch to add the hangout link uses calendarId: selectedCalendar. If no destination calendar matches the credentialId, selectedCalendar is undefined, so the event is created on 'primary' but the patch request is made with an undefined calendarId.

findings.title: Google deleteEvent fallback ignores destination calendar when externalCalendarId is missing
findings.body: GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent falls back to finding a destination calendar by comparing externalId to externalCalendarId even when externalCalendarId is undefined/null. That fallback cannot match, so deletion defaults to 'primary'. If the event was created on a non-primary calendar and the reference lacks externalCalendarId, deletion can target the wrong calendar and leave the event behind.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar for all hosts
findings.body: Office365CalendarService.createEvent selects only the first entry from event.destinationCalendar and builds the Graph URL from that externalId. CalendarManager may call createEvent once per host destination calendar/credential for collective events, but this implementation ignores the credential being used. For a second host, it will attempt to create the event in the first host's calendar, which can fail or create the event in the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar for all hosts
findings.body: LarkCalendarService.createEvent uses only event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId. When multiple host destination calendars are supplied for a collective event, CalendarManager creates one event per destination/credential, but Lark will repeatedly target the first host's calendar instead of the calendar associated with the credential being used. This prevents multiple hosts from receiving correct Lark calendar events.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent filters calendars by the first destination calendar only
findings.body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters listCalendars(event) using event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId. For multiple host destination calendars, a call for another host's credential will filter that host's calendars using the first host's externalId. If no calendar matches, no calendar object is created but the method still returns success, silently failing to create events for non-main hosts.

findings.title: Organization slug condition is inverted
findings.body: The organization creation data now includes slug when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true. The previous logic included slug when billing was disabled and stored requestedSlug in metadata when billing was enabled. This reversal means organizations may get a slug immediately when billing is enabled and may have no slug when billing is disabled, breaking the intended billing/organization provisioning flow.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes with all organizer credentials and first reference only
findings.body: In handleCancelBooking, when cancelling all remaining recurring events and a calendar reference has a credentialId, the code loops over all of the organizer's calendar credentials and deletes the first calendar reference found on each updated booking. It ignores the specific credentialId/externalCalendarId being processed and repeats this for every calendar reference. With multiple calendar references this causes duplicate or cross-credential delete attempts and can miss non-organizer credentials fetched from the DB.

findings.title: await apiDeletes does not await the queued deletion promises
findings.body: In the paid cancellation branch, apiDeletes is an array of promises from calendar/video deletion calls, but the code executes await apiDeletes. Awaiting an array does not wait for the promises inside it, so the handler can return before deletions complete and rejected promises may become unhandled. It should use Promise.all or Promise.allSettled on apiDeletes.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents can pass an undefined credential to updateEvent
findings.body: In EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents, if a booking reference has credentialId but the credential is not present in this.calendarCredentials and cannot be loaded from the database with an app slug, credential remains undefined. The code still calls updateEvent(credential, ...), causing the update to reject and all calendar updates to fail instead of skipping or reporting only the broken reference.
